source_caption:
For the film’s iconic stadium serenade, where Patrick Verona sings to Kat across the high school bleachers, Heath Ledger actually chose the song himself. The script originally called for Patrick to perform “I Think I Love You” by The Partridge Family or a track by The Righteous Brothers. Ledger strongly objected, arguing that the studio’s choices didn’t carry the necessary romantic weight or grand cinematic feel to convince the audience of his character’s apology. He personally campaigned for Frankie Valli’s “Can’t Take My Eyes Off You” instead. The studio agreed, and Ledger proceeded to spontaneously choreograph a significant portion of his own charismatic dance moves as he evaded the security guards, turning his musical suggestion into one of the most beloved and memorable romantic comedy sequences of the 1990s.

10 Things I Hate About You (1999), directed by Gil Junger, starring Julia Stiles, Heath Ledger, Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Larisa Oleynik. A modern high school adaptation of Shakespeare’s The Taming of the Shrew, where a new student pays a mysterious, rebellious outcast to date an abrasive, unsociable girl so that he can take her popular younger sister out on a date.

source_details.synopsis: 10 Things I Hate About You is a 1999 American teen romantic comedy directed by Gil Junger (in his directorial debut) from a screenplay by Karen McCullah Lutz and Kirsten Smith. Adapted from William Shakespeare's comedy The Taming of the Shrew, it stars Julia Stiles, Heath Ledger, Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Larisa Oleynik, Larry Miller, Andrew Keegan, David Krumholtz, Susan May Pratt, and Gabrielle Union. In the film, high-school student Cameron James (Gordon-Levitt) is unable to date sophomore Bianca Stratford (Oleynik) until her asocial feminist senior sister Kat (Stiles) dates, leading to Cameron recruiting bad boy classmate Patrick Verona (Ledger) to date Kat.
